slides.title: The roadmap: what this course will cover
slides.summary: Every topic the course aims to cover, in six areas, and how far along each area is.
body: This is the checklist for the whole course: the topics you need to understand how modern AI systems are built, from the model itself to the products around it.

ul: LLM concepts: how the model reads, thinks and writes.
RAG: letting a model look things up.
AI system design: serving models quickly and cheaply.
AI agents: models that use tools and act in steps.
AI security: attacks, and how to defend against them.

body: <mark class="info">A ticked topic links to the slide that teaches it; the rest are marked coming soon.</mark>
Pick an area on the right to see its topics.

slides.title: LLM concepts
slides.summary: How a language model reads text, works on it and writes an answer, and the settings that shape what it says.
body: This area covers the model itself: tokens, attention, the transformer, and what happens at each step of writing an answer.

Most of it is already in the LLM architecture section. Still to come are the prompting topics (few-shot prompting, structured outputs), images and audio as input, and the ways to make models smaller or adapt them: LoRA, QLoRA and distillation.
Tap a ticked topic to jump to the slide that teaches it.

slides.title: RAG
slides.summary: Retrieval-augmented generation: finding the right text and giving it to the model before it answers.
body: This area covers every step of a RAG system: cutting documents into chunks, turning them into vectors, searching, reranking, and checking the results.

The Retrieval-augmented generation chapter covers most of it. Still to come: getting clean text out of PDFs and web pages (document parsing), and parent-child chunking, which searches small chunks but hands the model the bigger section around them.

slides.title: AI system design
slides.summary: Running models in production: speed, cost, reliability and serving many users at once.
body: A model on its own is not a product. This area covers the engineering around it: which model handles each request, what happens when one fails, how answers stream back quickly, and how to keep the bill under control.
Caching and the KV cache are covered in Output & inference. Most of this area is still to come.

slides.title: AI agents
slides.summary: Models that use tools in a loop: planning, acting, checking their work and remembering.
body: An agent is a model that calls tools, reads the results and decides what to do next, again and again, until the task is done.

Tool calling is introduced in Assistant architecture, and skills in the AI-assisted engineering section. The rest, from the agent loop to MCP and multi-agent systems, is coming in the AI agents and Tools & MCP sections.

slides.title: Evals
slides.summary: How to measure whether an AI system gives good answers, and catch it when it gets worse.
body: You can't improve what you can't measure. Evals are tests for AI systems: a set of questions, a way to score the answers, and monitoring once real users arrive.
The RAG testing slide already covers test sets, faithfulness, answer relevance and LLM judges. Most of this area is coming in the Evals section.

slides.title: AI security
slides.summary: How AI systems that read untrusted text and use tools get attacked, and how to defend them.
body: Once a model reads untrusted text and can use tools, attackers can talk to it too.

Prompt injection, jailbreaks, safety classifiers and red-teaming are covered in Assistant architecture, and RAG permissions and poisoning in Retrieval-augmented generation. The engineering side (secrets, sandboxes, audit logs) is coming in the AI security section.
